title: Chemical Reactions
summary: Tell physical and chemical changes apart, recognise signs of a reaction, name reactants and products, and understand that atoms are rearranged but never created or destroyed.

rows: Usually difficult or impossible to reverse
Particles stay the same; only their arrangement or spacing changes
Atoms are rearranged into new molecules
Melting ice, dissolving sugar, tearing paper, boiling water
Burning wood, rusting, cooking an egg, baking a cake, digestion

notes.text: Signs that a chemical reaction has happened

items: A **gas** is given off (bubbles or fizzing).
A **colour change** that cannot easily be reversed.
A **precipitate** (an insoluble solid) forms when two solutions are mixed.
Energy is given off or taken in: the mixture becomes **hot** or **cold**, or light is produced.

notes.text: The substances you start with are the **reactants**; the new substances formed are the **products**. A reaction is written as an equation with the reactants on the left, an arrow (meaning *produces* or *forms*), and the products on the right.

notes.caption: The same reaction written with chemical formulae

notes.text: In a chemical reaction, the bonds between atoms break and new bonds form. Atoms are **rearranged**, but no atoms are created or destroyed. So the **total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products** (in a closed system). This is the **law of conservation of mass**.

notes.title: Counting atoms in a balanced equation
notes.problem: Show that atoms are conserved in: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
steps: Left: 2H₂ has 4 hydrogen atoms; O₂ has 2 oxygen atoms.
Right: 2H₂O has 2 × 2 = 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 × 1 = 2 oxygen atoms.
The same number of each kind of atom is on both sides, so the equation is balanced.
notes.answer: 4 H and 2 O on each side

notes.title: Using conservation of mass
notes.problem: 12 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen to form 20 g of magnesium oxide. What mass of oxygen reacted?
steps: mass of reactants = mass of products

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: When wood burns, the ash weighs less than the wood. Mass has not disappeared: the carbon dioxide and water vapour produced escaped into the air. In a sealed container, the total mass would stay the same.

rows: fuel + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ heat and light)
glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a chemical change?
What name is given to the substances you start with in a chemical reaction?
What is an insoluble solid that forms when two solutions react called?
In a chemical reaction, new atoms are created.
56 g of iron reacts completely with sulfur to form 88 g of iron sulfide. What mass of sulfur reacted?
In the equation CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, how many oxygen atoms are on the product side?
questions.explanation: CO₂ has 2 and 2H₂O has 2, so 4 in total.

questions.prompt: Which observation does NOT necessarily show that a chemical reaction has taken place?
options: Bubbles of a new gas form
A solid changes shape when cut

questions.prompt: Match each observation to the sign of a chemical reaction it shows.

pairs.left: Fizzing when vinegar is added to baking soda
A cloudy solid appears when two clear solutions are mixed
A copper roof slowly turns green

questions.prompt: A learner says that mass is lost when paper burns because the ash is lighter than the paper. Explain why this is incorrect.
questions.memo:
✓ Gases (carbon dioxide and water vapour) are produced and escape into the air (1)
✓ The total mass of all products equals the mass of the reactants (paper + oxygen); mass is conserved (1)

questions.prompt: State TWO differences between a physical change and a chemical change.
questions.memo:
✓ A chemical change forms a new substance; a physical change does not (1)
✓ Physical changes are usually easily reversed; chemical changes are not (1)
